plugin.name: RobustYaml
plugin.description:
RobustYaml teaches Rider the YAML prototypes of Robust Toolbox — the format the content of Space Station 14 is written in. It reads the C# of the engine and of the content, so what it knows about a key is what the game will do with that key.

  • Completion and validation for component names, prototype kinds, datafields, enum members, flags, colours, vectors, sprite states and prototype ids. Every value is judged by the rule the engine uses to read it, down to the difference between float and TimeSpan.
  • Navigation: Ctrl+click from parent: to the declaration, from type: Sprite to SpriteComponent.cs, from a resource path to the file, and from a C# string literal straight into the content. Find Usages and Rename cover prototype ids and localization keys across YAML, .ftl, .cs, XAML and the guidebook — in one refactoring, not file by file.
  • What the player will see: the sprite in the gutter and in the hover, the entity name and the text of a localization message as inline hints, the localized name, description and suffix of a prototype in the popup.
  • Editing: sequence indentation the way SS14 writes it, live templates, folding, Structure View, Ctrl+H over the inheritance chain, a colour picker for Robust hex.

Prototypes and Resources normally lie outside the solution — the plugin indexes them anyway, so everything works on a checkout opened the usual way.

The checks come from the engine's own serializers and are measured against a full content checkout: 30 000 prototypes and 56 000 localization messages, with the false positives driven to zero before a check ships.
